title: Homeland Security for Children Act
official_summary:
Homeland Security for Children Act

This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to ensure that the needs of children are considered in homeland security planning.

Specifically, each DHS office and component must take into account the needs of children, including children within underserved communities, in mission planning and execution. DHS must require each office and component to seek advice and feedback from organizations representing the needs of children.

The bill directs the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to identify and integrate the needs of children into activities to prepare for, protect against, respond to, recover from, and mitigate against the risk of natural disasters, acts of terrorism, and other disasters, including by appointing a technical expert to coordinate such integration.

summary.headline: A 2022 law requires the Department of Homeland Security and FEMA to consider children's needs in their emergency and security planning.
summary.what_it_does: The law tells the Department of Homeland Security to make sure children's needs are considered when it plans and carries out its missions. Each DHS office and component must account for children, including children in underserved communities. DHS must also ask groups that represent children for advice and feedback. FEMA must identify and build children's needs into its work on disasters and terrorism, and it must appoint a technical expert to coordinate this.

who_it_affects.group: Children and families in disaster-prone or underserved communities
who_it_affects.how: Federal emergency planning is directed to take their specific needs into account before, during, and after disasters and terrorism events.
DHS must seek their advice and feedback on homeland security and emergency planning.

who_it_affects.group: DHS offices and components, including FEMA
who_it_affects.how: They must add children's needs to mission planning and carry out a required coordination role with a designated technical expert.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was enacted on June 6, 2022, and the summary does not list separate later deadlines.
